clue.text: Stone from small workroom

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a lab (laboratory) is a room where scientific work is done

explanation.surface: A piece of stone carried away from a little workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A slab is a flat thick piece of stone, as used for paving.

clue.text: Old colonnade to be found in South Africa

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient covered walkway that can be seen in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a roofed portico with columns in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Cheek-and the area beneath it

definitions.meaning: cheek here is nerve or impudence, as in 'what a nerve'
the body part directly below the face's cheek

explanation.surface: Someone's face and the part just under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck can mean brazen nerve, and it is also the part of the body joining head to shoulders.

clue.text: Breaking a leg can require a setting agent

indicators.note: breaking the words apart lets their letters be put back in a new order

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A broken leg may need a plaster cast that sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges A LEG into GELA; 'require' just joins it to the definition. The surface suggests a cast, but the setting agent is a cooking gel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is what makes jellies firm, so it is a gelling or setting ingredient.

clue.text: Fine show of resistance at the racecourse

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for the structure found there

parts.note: grand means splendid or fine
to make a stand is to resist

explanation.surface: A splendid display of defiance at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it points to the thing found at a racecourse rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators watch the horses from the main covered stand of seating at a racecourse.

clue.text: Good luck to the elite

definitions.meaning: a parting wish for someone's success
the finest people or things, the cream

explanation.surface: Wishing fortune to the top people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common send-off wish, and it also names the very finest of a group.

clue.text: Great help rendered daily

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Somebody gave tremendous assistance every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges the letters of GREAT HELP. 'daily' is a noun here, a daily newspaper, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every day, and this is the paper printing the puzzle.

clue.text: Correct work is the target to aim for

definitions.meaning: to grade or assess pupils' work, as a teacher does
the goal or bullseye one shoots at

explanation.surface: Getting work right is the goal to strive for.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers mark homework, and a mark is also a target, as in 'hit the mark'.

clue.text: Leading party supported by doctor and butler

indicators.note: in a down answer the earlier piece sits on top of the one that holds it up

parts.note: major means chief or leading
a do is a party
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A top political party backed by a physician and a manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: A majordomo is the chief steward of a great household, the senior servant.

clue.text: Boycott letters containing menacing threats

parts.note: to black goods or a firm is to boycott them, as trade unions did
mail is letters sent by post

explanation.surface: Correspondence calling for a boycott carries intimidating demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is a link here, not an insertion: the two pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is extortion by intimidation, demanding money under the threat of exposure.

clue.text: Modest business is given Japanese currency

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business
Y is the symbol for the yen

explanation.surface: A small firm gets paid in yen.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means shy or bashful, reluctant to show oneself off.

clue.text: China vessel? Rubbish!

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed sailing ship from China
worthless stuff, trash

explanation.surface: Dismissing a piece of crockery as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A junk is a traditional Chinese sailing boat, and junk is also worthless clutter.

clue.text: eg, Love and self-esteem

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a nought shaped like O

explanation.surface: Examples such as affection and self-respect.
explanation.definitionFit: One's ego is one's sense of self-worth or self-importance.

clue.text: Relaxed and trouble-free departure

parts.note: easy means without difficulty
going is leaving, a departure

explanation.surface: A calm, smooth exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An easygoing person is laid-back and not easily upset.

clue.text: Got rid of a dire cadet in total disarray

indicators.note: being in complete disorder means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful military trainee is thrown out amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in total disarray' rearranges the letters of A DIRE CADET.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or eliminate completely.

clue.text: Getting established by incriminating others

definitions.meaning: founding or starting up something
framing someone, making an innocent person look guilty

explanation.surface: Building a position by framing other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting up a business is founding it; setting someone up is framing them.

clue.text: Acquire some clues to make one understand

parts.note: to get is to acquire
in a crossword, the across clues are one set of clues

explanation.surface: Collecting a few hints to help someone grasp something.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a point across is to communicate it so it is understood.

clue.text: Overcharge for matting material

definitions.meaning: to charge a customer too much, slang
a marsh plant whose stems are woven into mats

explanation.surface: Charging too much for floor mats.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush someone is informal for overcharging them, and rushes are plants woven into mats.

clue.text: Choral work may take so long

parts.note: can expresses permission, like may
ta-ta is a casual goodbye, like so long

explanation.surface: A piece for choir may take a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is only a link. 'so long' looks like duration but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition, often sacred, for soloists and choir.

clue.text: Uncle gets eggs right out of a Russian urn

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: A relative removes eggs from a Russian vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of a' is a link phrase, not a deletion; the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a metal urn traditionally used in Russia to heat water for tea.

clue.text: King depicted in sculpture is standing

indicators.note: a figure depicted in a carving sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a statue is a sculpture
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch shown in a carved figure is upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means reputation or status, one's standing.

clue.text: I am twice rebuffed by Rodolphe's darling

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests pushed back, so the letters are read backwards
twice says the contraction is written two times in a row

parts.note: contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor's sweetheart, said twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles IM to IMIM and 'rebuffed' turns it back. Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème, loved by the poet Rodolfo (Rodolphe in Murger's original novel).
explanation.definitionFit: In the opera the seamstress Mimi is the beloved of the poet Rodolphe.

clue.text: Slogan is just hearsay

definitions.meaning: a catchy phrase repeated for effect
to catch a word is merely to overhear it

explanation.surface: A motto that is merely rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a popular slogan; catching a word suggests picking something up by ear.

clue.text: Is imperfect

parts.note: read as grammar: the past tense of the verb 'is', the imperfect tense

explanation.definitionFit: The past form of the verb to be in the third person is the imperfect of 'is'.

clue.text: Negative point

definitions.meaning: a negating conjunction
a shortened form of north, a compass point, as in nor'wester

explanation.surface: A minus sign or a downside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor introduces a further negative, and nor' is a sailor's clipping of north, a point of the compass.

clue.text: A lot of criminals harbour some smouldering anger

indicators.note: to harbour some is to keep a portion inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bunch of crooks nursing a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'harbour' in the definition, but a band of crooks is not a harbour: 'harbour some' is the hiding signal and 'A lot of criminals' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is an organised group of lawbreakers.

clue.text: Immediately put in an awkward situation

definitions.meaning: at once, without delay
put in a difficult position, as when asked a hard question unexpectedly

explanation.surface: Being put on the defensive without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at once, and being put on it means being pressed for a quick answer.

clue.text: Hesitate over direction of flier

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: er is the sound of a speaker hesitating
NE is northeast, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Pausing over which way a pilot should go.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Places the British enter to knock back drink

indicators.note: entering puts one piece inside another
knocking back sends the word in the opposite direction, so its letters are reversed

parts.note: to sup is to drink
B is an abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Bars where Brits go to down a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock back' reverses SUP into PUS, and 'enter' puts B inside it. The surface makes 'knock back drink' sound like drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs are public houses, places where people go to drink; 'Places' stands for the plural noun.

clue.text: Friar giving sustenance to schoolchildren

definitions.meaning: Friar ... is Robin Hood's jovial companion
British school slang for food, especially snacks and sweets

explanation.surface: A monk providing food to pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is the outlaw band's monk in the Robin Hood legend, and tuck is old British boarding-school slang for food.

clue.text: Grass planted by a male representative

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A politician has planted some grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted by a' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is cannabis, and grass is slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Recoil at the passing of winter

definitions.meaning: to bounce back after being bent or pushed
read as two words: the season after winter has returned

explanation.surface: Flinching as winter ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring back is to rebound, and when winter passes the warmer season is back.
